answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. A rotating random sample of peers audits its transactions; proven double claims or fabricated work slash the stake and remove its voting weight. The stake is an anchor for accountability, not proof that an agent is honest. An ivory-colored badge or a copied kernel of code earns no extra identities: to mount a Sybil attack, the attacker must fund many independent locks and risks losing them all.
